question: After the readiness RFC lands, should OpenClaw adopt these four opt-in hosting profiles, include runtime activation identity in v1, and make packaged profile conformance release-blocking?
rationale: Those choices establish permanent product support promises, configuration semantics, security assertions, and release policy; technical correctness and proof cannot determine the intended scope on their own.

options.title: Stage the contract
options.body: Accept the four opt-in profiles and activation identity after readiness lands, but keep packaged conformance advisory until upgrade and security-boundary experience supports a release gate.

options.title: Accept full v1
options.body: Accept the catalog, activation identity, and release-blocking packaged conformance together as the initial support contract.

options.title: Defer standard profiles
options.body: Keep readiness configurable without an OpenClaw-owned named profile catalog until deployment-support demand or ownership becomes clearer.

recommendation.title: Stage the contract
recommendation.body: Accept the four opt-in profiles and activation identity after readiness lands, but keep packaged conformance advisory until upgrade and security-boundary experience supports a release gate.

likelyOwner.reason: The release-blocking portion intersects most directly with the merged stable-release-policy work, although broader product and security owners should participate.
